_note: Copy and configuration for the two internal menu concept routes, /internal/menu-concept-b2/ and /internal/menu-concept-b1/. Review routes only. Nothing here is shipping copy and nothing here is linked from the site.
_dataRule: THE DISH ROWS ARE NOT IN THIS FILE AND MUST NOT BE. Both routes render from menu.json through the same `dishesFor` filter the location pages use, scoped to east-village. The reference mockups in _reference/menu-concepts/ are a DESIGN reference; the data layer is the source of truth. Nothing was transcribed out of their HTML.
_prices:
PRICES ARE OFF on the review routes AND on all seven location pages. The client asked for prices off the main menu page and did not rule on location pages, so off is the default and the decision is Steve's.

THE DATA IS READY AND COMPLETE, which is the part worth knowing before deciding. Every featured dish at every room has a live price in that room's own src/_data/toastMenus/*.json, pulled 2026-08-04: Convoy 12 of 12, College Heights, Crown Point, East Village and Mercury 11 of 11, Plaza Bonita 7 of 7, Maui 7 of 7 once the trio is matched through an alias (Maui lists them as 'Tajima RED Ramen' rather than 'Tajima Red'). Turning prices on is a data job of wiring toastMenus to the row, not a template change.

DO NOT USE menu.json's `price` FIELD FOR THIS. It is a single stale brand price and _priceStatus marks it not for display. A per-location menu wants the per-location figure, which is exactly what makes this worth doing properly rather than flipping a flag.
_sectionOrnaments:
The ghosted brand mark behind each band. Rice takes ONIGIRI, which is the reference's own choice for that section and the one sprite icon that means rice.

SUSHI, MONTHLY SPECIAL, KIDS AND COMBO GET NONE, and that is the rule working rather than an omission. The sprite is twelve marks and every one is a ramen component, an izakaya dish or the wordmark: there is nothing for raw fish, nothing for a skewer, nothing for a child and nothing for a set meal. DESIGN_SYSTEM.md: where no icon matches, use none. The /menu/ Dessert heading and the four-card hero already set that precedent twice. A mark chosen because a band looked bare is decoration.
_barTones:
Spine tones. From the reference: izakaya black with cream type, ramen gold with black type, dessert black with GOLD type, and RED for rice, which the reference assigns and which this build could not use until rice had rows. It has twelve now.

THE REFERENCE ONLY HAS FOUR TONES AND THERE ARE EIGHT SECTIONS, so four sections reuse one. Reuse is fine; two touching bands wearing the same tone is not, because then the spine stops separating anything. The assignment below is checked against every room's real band sequence by a guard in eleventy.config.js that FAILS THE BUILD on an adjacent clash, so this is not eyeballed and cannot rot when a room's menu changes.

Worst case is Mercury, which renders all seven of its sections: ink, gold, red, ink, gold, ink-gold, red. No two touch.
_legend: Marks render ONLY from menu.json `dietary`. Nothing is inferred from a description. The mockups also show spicy, vegetarian and raw or undercooked marks; no field for any of those exists in menu.json, so they are named as missing rather than guessed at.

legend.label: Spicy
legend.note: Built with chili, and it shows. Heat can be dialled down at the counter.

legend.label: Vegan
legend.note: No meat, fish, dairy or egg.

legend.label: Vegetarian
legend.note: No meat or fish, but contains dairy or egg.

legend.label: Served raw or undercooked
legend.note: Eating raw or undercooked meat, poultry, seafood, shellfish or eggs may increase your risk of foodborne illness.

_footerSource: Every line below is already-approved copy from faq.json, which draws on CLIENT_FACTS.md. NOT transcribed from the mockups' fine print, which carries strings nobody has cleared.
footer: Soy, wheat, shellfish, egg and dairy are all present across the menu.
There is no gluten-free noodle in any bowl. Some dishes can be prepared without gluten, so ask the floor.
Tell your server about any allergy before you order.
_footerLastLine: The third line is the only sentence here not lifted verbatim from faq.json. It states the standing instruction a reader needs and makes no claim about the kitchen. If it needs to go, delete it; the first two carry the allergen facts on their own.
_previewPane: B1 only. Features one dish per section, and only where the photograph carries REVIEWED alt in photos.json. Every dish photograph in the manifest was shot at Convoy, so each pane says so on its face. photos.json _rule scopes ROOM photography to its own location; a photograph of a bowl is a photograph of that bowl wherever it was taken, and captioning it is how /happy-hour/ already handles the same situation. A section with no qualifying photograph collapses.
_legendRule: The legend lists all four marks because it is a legend: it tells a reader what a mark means if they see one. What DOES NOT happen is inferring the flag onto a dish. Only `dietary` in menu.json drives a mark, and that field is populated on two of fourteen rows, both vegan. `spicy`, `vegetarian` and `raw` have no field at all, so no dish carries those marks and a line under the legend says so.
_cuts: The mark that sits in the spine column on the divider above a section. Same sprite limit as the ornaments, so four sections divide with a plain rule and no mark. The rule still draws: a band with no cut mark is not a band with no divider, or Mercury's seven sections would run together. See the markless branch in components/menu-concept.njk.
_rollout: The B2 module is on all seven location pages as of 2026-09-14 through components/location-menu.njk, filtered per room by the same dishesFor call the concept routes use. One component, seven pages, no copies. A room whose filter returns nothing renders nothing; nothing hits that today, and Plaza Bonita and Maui render two bands rather than three because neither has a dessert row.
_sectionOrder:
The order every room renders its bands in, and it is the order the printed menus use: small plates, then bowls, then rice, then the raw counter, then the specials board, then dessert, with the kids and combo blocks last because only one room each carries them.

MOVED OUT OF THE TEMPLATE 2026-09-15. menu-concept.njk hardcoded three sections. A room can now render as many as it has: Mercury seven, Plaza Bonita three, the other four rooms four. A section with no rows for a room renders nothing, which is how Crown Point gets four bands and not eight.
_legendIcons: Each legend entry names the symbol it draws. Spicy uses the BRAND chili from src/_includes/icons/chili.svg, which is what the approved reference uses (it calls it #i-chili-pepper and the artwork is byte identical to ours). The hand-drawn #m-spicy that used to stand in for it was an unclosed outline: three open paths with the pepper's left flank never drawn, so it rendered as a hook with a detached spur. It looked like a legend-only bug because no dish carries a spicy value, so the legend is the only surface that ever drew it.
_missingFlags: REMOVED. It was a hardcoded list reading spicy, vegetarian, 'raw or undercooked', and the last of those was false: five sushi rows carry dietary:['raw'] and the mark renders above the sentence denying it. The footnote is computed from the rendered rows now, in _data/roomMenus.js.
